label: prop:positive-definite-dagger
title: Frobenius dagger is positive-definite
html:
A positive-definite dagger gives categorical states genuine squared lengths. Let (\mathbf{C}, A) be a quantum universe whose endomorphism ring \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R is an ordered field. Assume a Frobenius pairing with form \int_A, and an antipode S that is R-linear, involutive (S^2 = \mathrm{id}), anti-multiplicative (S(xy) = S(y)\,S(x)) and unital.

For a morphism f \colon \mathbf{1} \to A define the Frobenius dagger

  f^{\dagger} =  \int_A \circ\, \mu(S(f) \otimes -),

and the form h(f, g) = \int_A \mu(S(f) \otimes g), so that f^{\dagger} \circ f = h(f, f). Assume that h is positive definite: h(f, f) > 0 for every non-zero f \colon \mathbf{1} \to A. Write L_x for left multiplication by x \in A. Then:

  1. L_{S(x)} is the unique R-linear adjoint of L_x for h, that is h(L_x a, b) = h(a, L_{S(x)} b);
  2. the dagger L_x^{\dagger} = L_{S(x)} is involutive and reverses products on these operators, as an involutive structure requires; this is checked only on left multiplications: L_x^{\dagger\dagger} = L_x and (L_x L_y)^{\dagger} = L_y^{\dagger} L_x^{\dagger};
  3. on \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R the dagger is S, which is the identity there;
  4. f^{\dagger} \circ f > 0 for every non-zero f \colon \mathbf{1} \to A.

Item 4 is the positivity hypothesis on h read through f^{\dagger} \circ f = h(f, f). Requiring S to be R-linear and involutive restricts this formulation to formally real ordered scalar fields at the involutive point: over \mathbb{C}, R-linearity would give h(if, if) = -h(f, f) < 0, and on the coordinate algebra of \mathrm{SU}(2) and its non-involutive quantum deformations (S^2 \neq \mathrm{id}_A) one already has \int_{\mathrm{SU}(2)} S(\beta)\beta = 0. Over \mathbb{C} and for non-involutive Hopf \ast-algebras, the positive GNS dagger replaces S with a conjugate-linear \ast-involution a \mapsto a^* (satisfying (S \circ *)^2 = \mathrm{id}_A) and sesquilinear form h_*(f, g) = \int_A f^* g.
